'''Arie Bialostocki''' <!--(1948–)-->({{Langx|he|אריה ביאלוסטוקי}}) is an Israeli American mathematician with expertise and contributions in [[discrete mathematics]] and [[finite groups]].<ref name=retire /><ref name=bio />

==Education and career==
Arie received his BSc, MSc, and PhD (1984) from [[Tel-Aviv University]] in Israel.<ref name=bio>{{
cite journal|
last=Bialostocki|
first=Arie|
title=An Application of Elementary Group Theory to Central Solitaire|
journal=[[The College Mathematics Journal]]|
volume=29|
issue=3|
pages=208–212|
year=1998|
doi=10.1080/07468342.1998.11973941}}</ref> His dissertation was done under the supervision of Marcel Herzog.<ref name=mgp>{{
Citation|url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=40301|title=Arie Bialostocki
}} at the [[Mathematics Genealogy Project]]
</ref> After a year of postdoc at the [[University of Calgary]] in Canada, he took a faculty position at the [[University of Idaho]], becoming a full professor in 1992.<ref name="bio" /> Arie retired from his position at the University of Idaho in 2011.<ref name=retire>
{{Cite web|url=https://issuu.com/uidaho/docs/math-news-11-12/3 |title=Professor Arie Bialostocki retires|date=2023-05-22}}
</ref>  He maintained strong international connections, corresponding with mathematicians from India, Kashmir, Iran, Jordan, and China.<ref name="retire" /> His [[Erdős number]] is 1.<ref name=erdos>
{{
cite journal|
last1=Bialostocki|
first1=Arie|
last2=Erdős|
first2=Paul|
last3=Lefmann|
first3=Hanno|
title=Monochromatic and zero-sum sets of nondecreasing diameter |
journal=[[Discrete Mathematics (journal)|Discrete Mathematics]]|
volume=137|
issue=1–3|
pages=19–34|
year=1995
| doi=10.1016/0012-365X(93)E0148-W | doi-access=free}}</ref> He has supervised seven PhD students and numerous undergraduate students who enjoyed his colorful anecdotes and advice.<ref name=retire /> He organized a summer [[Research Experience for Undergraduates]] (REU) program at the University of Idaho from 1999 to 2003 and maintained contact with many of the students who participated, some of whom went on to pursue their own careers in research.<ref name=retire />

==Mathematics research==
Arie has published more than 50 publications.<ref name=zb>
{{
Citation|url=https://zbmath.org/authors/bialostocki.arie|title=Arie Bialostocki
}} at [[zbMATH Open]]</ref><ref name=gs>
{{
Citation|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=5b0bYQsAAAAJ|title=Arie Bialostocki
}} at [[Google scholar]]</ref> Some of Bialostocki's contributions include:

* Bialostocki<ref name=inj1982>{{
cite journal|
last=Bialostocki|
first=Arie|
title=Nilpotent injectors in symmetric groups|
journal=[[Israel Journal of Mathematics]]|
volume=41|
issue=3|
pages=261–273|
year=1982
| doi=10.1007/BF02771725|
s2cid=122321992}}</ref> redefined<ref name=nilpo>{{
Citation|url=https://zbmath.org/0492.20003|title=Review
}} by A. R. Camina at [[zbMATH Open]]</ref> a <math>B</math>-injector in a [[finite group]] G to be any maximal nilpotent subgroup <math>B</math> of <math>G</math> satisfying <math>d_2(B)=d_2(G)</math>, where <math>d_2(X)</math> is the largest cardinality of a subgroup of <math>G</math> which is nilpotent of class at most <math>2</math>. Using his definition, it was proved by several authors<ref name=y2>{{
cite journal|
last=Sheu|
first=Tsung-Luen|
title=Nilpotent injectors in general linear groups|
journal=[[Journal of Algebra]]|
volume=160|
issue=2|
pages=380–418|
year=1993
| doi=10.1006/jabr.1993.1192 | doi-access=free}}</ref><ref name=y3>{{
cite journal|
last1=Mohammed|
first1=Mashhour Ibrahim|
title=On nilpotent injectors of Fischer group <math>M(22)</math>|
journal=Hokkaido Mathematical Journal|
volume=38|
issue=4|
pages=627–633|
year=2009
| doi=10.14492/hokmj/1258554237 | doi-access=free}}</ref><ref name=y4>{{
cite journal|
last=Flavell|
first=Paul|
title=Nilpotent injectors in finite groups all of whose local subgroups are N-constrained|
journal=[[Journal of Algebra]]|
volume=149|
issue=2|
pages=405–418|
year=1992
| doi=10.1016/0021-8693(92)90024-G | doi-access=free}}</ref><ref name=y5>{{
cite journal|
last1=Alali|
first1=M. I. M.|
last2=Hering|
first2=Ch.|
last3=Neumann|
first3=A.|
title=More on B-injectors of sporadic groups|
journal=[[Communications in Algebra]]|
volume=28|
issue=4|
pages=2185–2190|
year=2000
| doi=10.1080/00927870008826951|
s2cid=120962734}}</ref> that in many non-solvable groups the nilpotent injectors form a unique conjugacy class.

* Bialostocki contributed  to the generalization of the [[Erdős-Ginzburg-Ziv theorem]] (also known as the [[EGZ theorem]]).<ref name=bl92>{{
cite book|
last1=Bialostocki|
first1=A.|
last2=Lotspeich|
first2=M.|
contribution=Some developments of the Erdős-Ginzburg-Ziv theorem I|
title=Sets, graphs, and numbers: a birthday salute to Vera T. Sós and András Hajnal
| series=Colloquia mathematica Societatis János Bolyai|
pages=97–117|
year=1992
}}</ref><ref name=bl2003>{{
cite journal|
last1=Bialostocki|
first1=Arie|
last2=Dierker|
first2=Paul|
last3=Grynkiewicz|
first3=David|
last4=Lotspeich|
first4=Mark|
title=On some developments of the Erdős-Ginzburg-Ziv theorem II|
journal=[[Acta Arithmetica]]|
volume=110|
issue=2|
pages=173–184|
year=2003
| doi=10.4064/aa110-2-7 |
bibcode=2003AcAri.110..173B| doi-access=free}}</ref> <!--Given <math>k \in \{1,2,\ldots, m\}</math>, let <math>g(m, k)</math> (respectively, <math>g^*(m,k)</math>) denote the least integer <math>g</math> such that every sequence of <math>g</math> integers modulo <math>m</math>, with <math>g \geqslant m</math>, belonging to at least (respectively, exactly) <math>k</math> classes contains a subsequence that satisfies <math>a_{i_1}+a_{i_2}+\cdots+a_{i_m}\equiv 0\pmod{m}</math>. The [[EGZ theorem]] is a special case with <math>g(m,2)=2m-1</math>. A key theorem coauthored by Bialostocki<ref name=bl92></ref><ref name=bl2003></ref> is: Given <math>m\geqslant k \geqslant 2</math> be positive integers, if <math>k</math> is even and  <math>m \geqslant k^2-2k-4</math>, or if <math>k</math> is odd and <math>m \geqslant k^2-2k-3</math>, then (a) <math>g(m,k)=2m-\lfloor{(k^2-2k+5)/4} \rfloor</math>, (b) <math>g^*(m,k)=g(m,k)</math>. --> He conjectured: if <math>A=(a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_n)</math> is a sequence of elements of <math>{\mathbb Z}_m</math>, then <math>A</math> contains at least <math>{\lfloor{n/2}\rfloor \choose {m}}+{\lceil{n/2}\rceil \choose{m}}</math> zero sums of length <math>m</math>. The [[EGZ theorem]] is a special case where <math>n=2m-1</math>. The conjecture was partially confirmed by [[Mark Kisin|Kisin]],<ref name=kisin>{{
cite journal|
last=Kisin|
first=M.|
title=The number of zero sums modulo m in a sequence of length n|
journal=[[Mathematika]]|
volume=41|
issue=1|
pages=149–163|
year=1994
| doi=10.1112/S0025579300007257}}</ref> [[Zoltán Füredi|Füredi]] and [[Daniel Kleitman|Kleitman]],<ref name=fk>{{
cite book
| last1=Füredi | first1=Z. | authorlink1=Zoltán Füredi
| last2=Kleitman | first2=D. J. | authorlink2=Daniel Kleitman
| title=Combinatorics, Paul Erdős is eighty (volume 1)
| contribution=The minimal number of zero sums
| series=Bolyai Society Mathematical Studies 
| publisher=[[János Bolyai Mathematical Society]]
| pages=159–172
| year=1993}}</ref> and Grynkiewicz.<ref name=djg>{{
cite journal|
last1=Grynkiewicz|
first1=David J.|
title=On the number of <math>m</math>-term zero-sum subsequences|
journal=[[Acta Arithmetica]]|
volume=121|
issue=3|
pages=275–298|
year=2006
| doi=10.4064/aa121-3-5 |
bibcode=2006AcAri.121..275G| doi-access=free}}</ref>

* Bialostocki introduced the EGZ polynomials and contributed to generalize  the [[EGZ theorem]] for higher degree polynomials.<ref name=bl>{{
cite journal|
last1=Bialostocki|
first1=Arie|
last2=Luong|
first2=Tran Dinh|
title=Cubic symmetric polynomials yielding variations of the Erdős-Ginzburg-Ziv theorem|
journal=[[Acta Mathematica Hungarica]]|
volume=142|
pages=152–166|
year=2014
| doi=10.1007/s10474-013-0346-4|
s2cid=254240326}}</ref><ref name=abpv>{{
cite journal|
last1=Ahmed|
first1=Tanbir|
last2=Bialostocki|
first2=Arie|
last3=Pham|
first3=Thang|
last4=Vinh|
first4=Le Anh|
title=Power sum polynomials as relaxed EGZ polynomials|
journal=[[Integers]]|
volume=19|
pages=A49|
year=2019
| url=http://math.colgate.edu/~integers/t49/t49.pdf}}</ref> The [[EGZ theorem]] is associated with the first degree elementary polynomial.

* Bialostocki and Dierker<ref name=bd1990>{{

year=1990}}</ref><ref name=bd1992>{{cite journal|

* Bialostocki, [[Paul Erdős|Erdős]], and Lefmann<ref name=erdos /> introduced<ref name=rev_erdos>{{
Citation|url=https://zbmath.org/0822.05046|title=Review }} by [[Ralph Faudree]] at [[zbMATH Open]]</ref> the relationship of [[EGZ theorem]] to [[Ramsey Theory]] on the positive integers.

* In Jakobs and [[Dieter Jungnickel|Jungnickel]]'s book "Einführung in die Kombinatorik",<ref name=nullsom>{{
cite book|
last1=Jakobs|
first1=Conrad|
last2=Jungnickel|
first2=Dieter|
title=Einführung in die Kombinatorik |
publisher=de Gruyter Lehrbuch|
isbn= 3-11-016727-1|
year=2004
| doi=10.1515/9783110197990}}</ref> Bialostocki and Dierker are attributed for introducing [[Zero-sum Ramsey theory]]. In Landman and [[Aaron Robertson (mathematician)|Robertson]]'s book "Ramsey Theory on the Integers",<ref name=rti>{{
cite book|
last1=Landman|
first1=Bruce|
last2=Robertson|

title=Ramsey Theory on the Integers
| edition=Second

| volume=73
| publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]|
isbn= 978-0-8218-9867-3|
date=2015
}}</ref> the number <math>b(m, k; r)</math> is defined in honor of Bialostocki's contributions to the [[Zero-sum Ramsey theory]].
